title: Ancient Rome's Painted City Is Finally Open
mediaSource: ancient Rome Painted City fresco Great Mosaic Baths of Trajan

scenes.title: A giant city was painted on a Roman wall
scenes.narration: Near the Colosseum, one of ancient Rome's largest known fresco and mosaic complexes has opened to the public for the first time.
keywords: Painted City Rome fresco Baths of Trajan

scenes.title: It took about 30 years to open
scenes.narration: The artworks were discovered during excavations in the 1990s, but preservation and restoration kept them closed for decades.

scenes.title: The wall shows an entire seaside city
scenes.narration: The fresco depicts walls, buildings, theaters, and temples in a maritime city viewed almost like a map from above.

scenes.title: The mosaic rises about 15 meters
scenes.narration: The accompanying Great Mosaic reaches roughly 15 meters high, revealing the huge scale of Roman decorative art.

scenes.title: Roman baths were more than baths
scenes.narration: The Baths of Trajan also included spaces such as a grand library, showing that bath complexes served as major social and cultural centers.

scenes.title: A 2,000-year-old city view is visible again
scenes.narration: Buildings alone cannot show us everything about Roman urban life. This wall painting preserves a rare visual record of how an ancient city was imagined.
